data.narrative:
ARC Clean Technology is a Series G nuclear energy company that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 8 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private firms (Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy) operating in the same sector.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($50M+) as a proxy for entry valuation, a $14M base value is escalated by a 1.25x multiplier typical for Series G advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $18M. Peer-median valuation is not applicable; while 5 nuclear energy comps exist, none meet the narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparability, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for robust median anchoring.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $21M, with a median estimate of $18M. This single-method triangulation carries material uncertainty. The primary constraint is insufficient granular peer comparability in the nuclear energy sector at Series G; a denser peer set at adjacent stages or similar capital-raise levels would strengthen conviction in the range. Founder track record and technology differentiation relative to the comp set warrant qualitative assessment but are not quantified in this analysis.
